citation: Thompson, D.W. (1917). On Growth and Form, Ch. XVII, pp. 752-753, Fig. 383
claim_text: The skulls of crocodiles (C. porosus, C. americanus, Notosuchus terrestris) are mutually transformable by coordinate deformation.

state_variables.landmarks: 78 homologous 3D cranial landmarks per specimen (Watanabe & Slice 2014)
state_variables.projection: Lateral view uses anteroposterior (x) and dorsoventral (z) coordinates after per-specimen GPA centering and scaling

governing_transforms.name: Moebius coaxial
governing_transforms.formula: z' = z / (1 - c z) in complex lateral plane

boundary_conditions: Species-mean shapes after GPA; extant adult/juvenile mix in ontogeny dataset; Notosuchus not represented

parameter_regime.note: used as upper envelope of flexible deformation

empirical_claims: Cross-species warp RMSE should not exceed within-species (C. porosus) leave-one-out noise floor if mutual transformability holds
Notosuchus terrestris requires fossil landmarks not present in Dryad 14fn1
